You built yourself a more demanding job. But the problem isn't your work ethic. It's the model. You're trading your time for money, and you're running out of time. The shift happens when you decide to stop being the engine and start building the engines. Using simple AI and automation, you can create systems that run for you. This is the entire idea behind 'Build Online, Live Offline.' You build the machine once so that you can get back to your life. If you're at that point, comment 'FieldWork' below. I'll send you the roadmap to build a business that actually serves your life.
script: Hook: Start with the quiet realization that 'it's over'.
Problem: Define 'it' as realizing your business is a cage, not a vehicle for freedom.
Insight: The issue isn't hard work, it's a broken model of trading time for money.
Solution: Stop being the engine and start building automated systems.
Vision: Introduce the 'Build Online, Live Offline' philosophy.
CTA: Comment 'FieldWork' for the roadmap.
guidance: Film as a simple, grounded talking head shot, maybe in a comfortable chair or leaning against a desk. Keep the background clean and warm.
Use the hook as a bold, centered text overlay for the first 3-4 seconds to stop the scroll.
When you say 'Live Offline,' cut to 2-3 seconds of B-roll showing you outdoors, with family, or doing something you love. This visually represents the payoff.
End with a clear text overlay on the screen: 'Comment “FIELDWORK”'.
Use a trending, slightly reflective or somber audio track that fits the initial mood, but make sure your voice is the primary audio.

items.headline: The Question We Need To Ask
items.angle: Pose a single, powerful 'what if' question that contrasts the 'build online' grind with the 'live offline' dream. This will surface the core anxiety FieldWork solves: the fear of building a business that costs you your life.
hooks: What if we build the whole thing online, just to realize we forgot how to live offline?
What if we spend our best years building the business, and miss the years we can't get back?
What if the 'someday' adventures we're working for never happen because we are always working?
What if we automate everything in our business except for the time we spend with the people we love?
What if we get to the top of the mountain and realize we forgot why we started climbing?
talking_points: I want you to really think about this for a second: What if we build this whole thing online, just to realize we completely forgot how to live offline?
It is the great paradox for so many founders and experts I talk to.
You start building a business to create freedom, but you end up chained to a laptop, answering emails at dinner, and pushing those big trips off for 'next quarter'.
Your life becomes something that happens in the margins of your work.
But the truth is, the business is supposed to serve your life, not the other way around.
That shift only happens when you intentionally design it to.
It happens when you build the right engines, using smart automation and AI, that work for you so you do not have to.
This is how you build a business that buys back your time, so you can spend it out in the field, living the life you were working for all along.
If this idea resonates with you, I put together a guide on how we do this. Just comment the word 'FIELD' below and I will send it over.
